# Levels 0.1.10 beta
A more compact mixer with clearer per-app controls.
## What changed
- Narrower output selectors fit the selected device name. Long device names wrap instead of using abbreviations. - Smaller mixer panel with tighter side padding and less space between apps. Text remains readable and volume slider travel stays consistent. - Mute and reset sit together below each app's volume slider, beside its output selector. - Master and app percentages share an aligned column; the master percentage remains larger. - Light, dark, Solid, and Liquid Glass appearances keep the same layout.
## Install or update
Choose Options → Updates → Check for Updates. The downloadable beta DMG contains the same app. Updates are verified with Levels' signing key and installation requires approval. Existing automatic-check preferences and update indicators are preserved.
This release keeps the same Apple Development signing certificate as 0.1.9. It does not reset audio permissions or change the audio engine. Saved volume, mute, output, and appearance choices are retained. It is not Apple-notarized; a first browser-downloaded launch may still require [Apple's Open Anyway approval](https://support.apple.com/102445).
## Requirements and validation
Apple silicon, macOS 15+. Liquid Glass requires macOS 26+. Audio is processed locally, never saved or uploaded.
All 95 regression tests passed. Native layout checks cover dark/light and Solid/Liquid Glass, full and wrapped output names, route selection, and Settings open/close cycles. Broader Bluetooth, external monitor, and sleep/wake listening tests remain pending.
Built by heyjoseluna. Inspired by Ahmed Gagan. MIT and Sparkle notices are included.

# Levels 0.1.9 beta
Pausing Spotify or another audio app no longer leaves its controls blocked.
## What changed
- Idle apps and stopped audio engines are treated as normal pauses. Native playback stays available; fresh samples reapply the saved volume when playback resumes. - Genuine tap or device failures restore native playback and retry automatically, with a delay that increases up to 30 seconds if a driver keeps failing. You do not need to move the slider or reset the app. - Recovery is independent for each app. New audio helpers reconnect immediately. Reset, quit and sleep cancel obsolete retries. - During a genuine failure, the status says Reconnecting. Saved volume, mute and output choices are retained. - The watchdog checks less frequently than 0.1.8 while keeping the silent-playback safeguards.
## Install or update
Choose Options → Updates → Check for Updates. The same tested app is in the downloadable beta DMG. Updates are verified with Levels' signing key and installation requires approval.
This release keeps the same Apple Development signing certificate as 0.1.8. It does not reset audio permissions or scan paired Bluetooth devices on startup. macOS controls permission persistence. It is not Apple-notarized; a first browser-downloaded launch may still require [Apple's Open Anyway approval](https://support.apple.com/102445).
## Requirements and privacy
Apple silicon, macOS 15+. Liquid Glass requires macOS 26+. Per-app audio adjustment requires System Audio Recording permission. Audio is processed locally, never saved or uploaded. Automatic checks preserve existing opt-outs; the white update indicator remains available.
Regression checks cover pause/resume grace, silent streams, delayed retries, independent apps and helper replacement. Native hardware tests exercise an engine stop/resume and an injected active callback stall. Broader Bluetooth, external monitor and sleep/wake listening tests remain pending.
Built by heyjoseluna. Inspired by Ahmed Gagan. MIT and Sparkle notices are included.

# Levels 0.1.8 beta
Safe audio handoff, a compact mixer, and quiet update notifications.
## What changed
- Startup no longer mutes native playback before the replacement audio path delivers real samples. Stalled callbacks release the tap and restore native playback; saved levels and routes are retained. - Process taps use their own appended input buffer rather than a physical microphone stream. Passive meters remain nonmuting. - This beta uses the owner’s stable Apple Development certificate. The first switch may require audio access approval once; later builds keep the same signing identity. It is not Apple-notarized.
- A small white update-available dot appears on the menu-bar icon and Options button. The Updates menu offers the available version. Scheduled checks use a gentle indicator; manual checks open the install dialog. - Automatic update checks are enabled for new installs. Existing choices, including an explicit opt-out, are preserved. Installation still requires approval. - Full selected-output names appear in wider thin buttons below each app slider. Playback status sits beside the app name and uses Playing/Idle wording, while mute and zero-volume states remain distinct. - San Francisco typography for Master volume; the larger master percentage shares the app-percentage column. Sliders retain their travel and aligned controls. - Ordinary volume, routing, startup, sleep recovery and device-change handling no longer scan paired Bluetooth devices. Connected Bluetooth outputs remain available through Core Audio. Direct Bluetooth access waits for an explicit connect/disconnect action. - Saved volume, mute, routing and appearance choices are retained.
## Install or update
Already using a connected beta (0.1.5 or later)? Choose Options → Updates → Check for Updates. Daily checks are optional, and installation requires your approval. Saved volume, mute, routing, and appearance choices are retained. Update archives are verified with Levels' dedicated signing key.
First install: download the beta DMG, drag Levels to Applications, eject the image, and open Levels. The DMG includes an Open Privacy & Security shortcut to make Apple's first-launch approval easier to reach. Levels lives in the menu bar; Settings opens only when requested.
**Zero-budget, not Apple-notarized.** macOS may block a browser-downloaded first launch. If you trust Levels, follow [Apple's Open Anyway instructions](https://support.apple.com/102445). A free ad-hoc or updater signature cannot replace Apple notarization. Managed Macs may restrict approval. No system security setting is disabled.
## Requirements and privacy
Apple silicon, macOS 15+. Native Liquid Glass requires macOS 26+. Per-app controls and signal detection need System Audio Recording permission. Audio is processed locally and never saved or uploaded. Passive measurement exists only while the mixer is visible and does not mute or reroute native playback. A process with an adjusted level or route still needs its control tap while Levels is running. Quitting restores native playback.
## Beta testing
Automated checks cover independent reset, saved preferences, silent audio, signal detection, helper churn, limiter behavior, and existing audio regressions. Physical HDMI/DisplayPort keyboard controls, Bluetooth codec quality, and broader hardware sleep/wake testing remain pending.
Report bugs at https://github.com/madetonight/Levels/issues with Mac model, macOS version, devices, and reproduction steps. Please do not upload private recordings.
Built by heyjoseluna. Inspired by Ahmed Gagan. MIT and Sparkle notices are included.

# Levels 0.1.7 beta
A compact mixer with thinner output buttons, shorter sliders, and a quieter app list.
## What changed
- Thin, flat output buttons show each app's selected device. Full names and the system-default choice remain available in the native menu and tooltip. - Smaller master-volume and microphone-gain percentages sit directly beside their sliders. - Compact, aligned app rows with a reset icon on the right of the slider. Reset restores the level from Settings (100% initially), preserving mute and output choices. - Shorter slider travel, with a slightly thicker track and thumb. Per-app range remains 0–200%, with limiting above 100%. - Browsers and common playback apps remain directly available. Other idle audio processes appear in a collapsed Other apps drawer; producing sound promotes an app into the main list, with a short grace period to avoid flicker. - Known apps remain available throughout their open session even if an audio helper disappears. Cached helpers cannot create controls for obsolete process IDs. - Scrolling works without visible scrollbars. # Levels 0.1.6 beta
A cleaner menu-bar mixer with independent app reset and more accurate playback status.
## What changed
- Reset below each app slider, on the right. Choose its default level in Settings → App volumes; it starts at 100%. Reset preserves mute and output choices. - Minimal Output and Input tabs without divider lines or the app counter. - Playing now uses real audio signal activity when measurement is available. Silent open streams show Idle; if measurement is unavailable, the honest fallback is Output active. - Short pauses and browser audio-helper replacements retain the row briefly. Alphabetical ordering keeps apps from jumping when playback changes. - A dedicated Settings window for device selection, login, inactive apps, monitor volume, Bluetooth microphone preference, and reset preferences. Appearance and Updates remain in the Options menu. - Per-app boost up to 200% with a peak limiter; optional software volume and keyboard support for fixed HDMI/DisplayPort outputs; optional Mac microphone preference for Bluetooth headphones.

# Levels 0.1.5 beta
A compact macOS menu-bar mixer for per-app volume, mute, and separate audio outputs.
**Requirements:** Apple silicon Mac, macOS 15 or later. Native Liquid Glass requires macOS 26 or later.
## Download and install
Download `Levels-0.1.5-beta-arm64.dmg`, open it, and drag Levels to Applications. Quit any previous copy before replacing it. Eject the image and launch Levels from Applications. It lives in the menu bar; no main window opens automatically.
**This beta is not Apple-notarized.** It uses a free ad-hoc signature, so macOS normally blocks the first launch of an internet download. If you trust the download, follow [Apple's instructions](https://support.apple.com/102445): attempt to open Levels, then visit System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway and confirm. Approval may be restricted on managed Macs.
## Changes in this sample
- Fixed the packaged ad-hoc beta failing to load its Sparkle framework at launch. - Connected in-app update checks to the public Levels update feed. - Optional daily checks; each installation requires your approval. - Removed the Apps section heading for a cleaner Output panel.
## Features
- Per-app volume and mute, with remembered settings. - Different output devices for different apps, including simultaneous playback. - Master output selection and volume; input selection and supported microphone gain. - Solid or Liquid Glass surfaces; light or dark appearance. - The same Options menu from the panel or a right-click on the menu-bar icon.
## Audio access
macOS System Audio Recording permission is needed for per-app control. Audio is processed locally, never saved or uploaded. macOS displays its privacy indicator while access is active. Levels must stay running for adjusted app levels to apply. Quitting restores native playback and can make a muted or reduced-volume app louder.
## Beta status and feedback
Sleep/wake recovery and external-device reconnection still need broader testing. Multiple-output playback and independent controls were verified on the development Mac; compatibility on other Macs and a fresh browser-downloaded installation remain unverified.
Install this first connected beta manually if you have 0.1.4 or earlier. Future releases appear in Options → Updates → Check for Updates. Enable Automatically check for updates for daily checks. Levels asks before installing; update archives are verified with its dedicated signing key. No purchase activation or subscription is required.
Report bugs at https://github.com/madetonight/Levels/issues with your macOS version, Mac model, audio devices, and steps to reproduce. For sleep bugs, include whether quitting Levels restores audio. Do not attach private audio recordings.
Built by heyjoseluna. Inspired by Ahmed Gagan. Upstream MIT and Sparkle notices are included in the DMG and app.
